newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS NEUTRAL ON AEX.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS NEUTRAL ON AEX.

text.p: Dutch chartists are again
largely neutral on the outlook for the AEX index this week,
though most see some short-term selling pressures weighing on
the index.
"A minor downtrend is developing on the charts of the AEX.
All in all, current technicals confirm the AEX is in a
corrective phase," said ING Barings."But we believe this will be
only a minor retracement of the market's recent strong gains."
The AEX index ended at 581.31 points on Friday, 8.9 points
below the previous Friday. In the week before that the index had
shed 4.15 points.
Fibonacci said the intermediate term trend still seemed
to be up. "We expect this trend to remain positive till
December."
And ABN AMRO said their outlook remained neutral. "Within
these levels we don't see anything substantial happening."

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.
Fibonacci Press -- The intermediate term trend still seems
to be up. The expected short term moderate weakness managed to
breach 575.8 last week and turned up. Though still under
pressure (support at 578), we expect this trend to remain
positive till December. Only a violation of the 572/570 area
will force a change of opinion, as this area is likely to change
the intermediate term trend also. So, significant danger for
long positions lies at 572/570.
ING Barings -- A minor downtrend is developing on the charts
of the AEX. Recent string of falling peaks (mid October at 597,
end October at 591 and last Friday at 585) suggests some selling
pressure kicking in at price rallies...Falling momentum confirms
the AEX's bearish stance. Money flow indicators show a flat
pattern, which is a neutral condition. It indicates that though
there is selling pressure, it is subdued. Market breadth
indicators are eroding a bit, but do not look critical. Market
breadth (A/D lines) shows that currently there is no leadership
in the market. All in all, current technicals confirm the AEX is
in a corrective phase.
However money flow as well as A/D lines do not look
dramatically bearish. Therefore we believe this will be only a
minor retracement of the market's recent strong gains. Our
bullish long term outlook remains intact as long as the market
stays above its 200-day moving average around 545. Long term
objectives unchanged at 630-635.
ABN AMRO -- After testing the very important support level
at 579 several times in a row, the AEX is now situated in a
broad range between 579 and 588. Between these levels we don't
see anything substantial happening and take volatile moves into
account. So for the short term, we advise to stay Neutral.
Depending on the side where the breakout occurs we have two
scenarios in mind. If prices drop below 579 we expect them to
fall towards 572 in the first place and if the bears prove to be
strong enough, even to 562. On the other hand, if prices rise
above 588, we expect an attack on 592.If prices rise above that
level a strong bullish signal will be provided.
The head and shoulders failure pattern will be a fact. In
any case the longer term outlook stays bullish as long as 550
stays intact. All together we advise to stay neutral until a
clear direction is chosen.
